declarations.docstring: A nonidentity auxiliary permutation sends the permutation attached to a tableau, after inverse left multiplication, to a class different from the tableau's class.
Assigns a subgroup of permutations of `Fin n` to each partition-indexed tableau.
A permutation lying in both auxiliary permutation collections is the identity.
An auxiliary type indexed by a natural number and a partition of it.
A second auxiliary type indexed by a natural number and a partition of it.
An auxiliary setoid on permutations of a finite type, indexed by a partition.
Membership in the auxiliary permutation collection relates a tableau permutation to its inverse translate.
A nonidentity member of the auxiliary permutation collection is strictly related to the corresponding inverse translate of a tableau permutation.
From a nonzero value on a member of a finite tableau set, one can select another nonzero member whose related nonzero members have the same tableau class.
Every pointed finite set of partition-indexed classes contains a member such that any related member of the set is equal to it.
The number of partition-indexed tableaux is bounded by the complex finrank of the indicated subtype.
An auxiliary proposition whose internal statement is unavailable.
Maps a permutation of `Fin n` into the second partition-indexed auxiliary type.
Left multiplication by an auxiliary permutation changes its associated vector by the permutation's sign.
The vector associated with a tableau permutation equals the vector assigned directly to the tableau.
Provides a finite type structure on the first partition-indexed auxiliary type.
A permutation belongs to the tableau-associated subgroup exactly when it is obtained by conjugating an auxiliary permutation by the tableau permutation.
Assigns an element of the second partition-indexed auxiliary type to each tableau.
A nonzero coefficient of a tableau vector at a permutation class forces the tableau permutation to be related to that permutation.
A tableau vector takes the value one at its own tableau class.
The family of tableau vectors is linearly independent over the complex numbers.
Every tableau vector lies in the image of the scalar-restricted auxiliary submodule under the indicated linear map.
A nonzero tableau-vector coefficient at another tableau's class forces the two tableau permutations to be related.
Conjugating a member of the tableau-associated subgroup by the tableau permutation yields a member of the auxiliary permutation collection.
Assigns a natural-number index to each position of a partition-indexed tableau.
Maps each partition-indexed tableau into the first auxiliary partition-indexed type.
The map from tableaux to their auxiliary classes is injective.
A natural-number statistic of a permutation, a finite index, and an additional natural-number parameter.
Equal permutation classes have equal values of the indexed permutation statistic.
An auxiliary binary relation on permutations, indexed by a partition.
Two permutations related in both directions determine equal auxiliary classes.
Along a two-step relation chain, equality of the endpoint classes forces equality of the middle and final classes.
The auxiliary permutation relation is preserved when either argument is replaced by one with the same class.
The auxiliary relation holds from every permutation to itself.
The auxiliary relation is transitive on permutations.
A complex-linear map from an auxiliary source to the second partition-indexed auxiliary type.
The linear map sends the distinguished auxiliary source element to the cardinality scalar times the basis vector at the identity class.
On the indicated auxiliary submodule, a vector with zero image under the linear map is itself zero.
If a vector maps to zero, then every left multiple of it also maps to zero.
If a vector maps to zero, then left multiplication by any permutation monomial still maps to zero.
The linear map sends the monomial of a permutation to the unit basis vector at the inverse permutation's class.
Left multiplication by a permutation is carried to reindexing by the inverse class action under the linear map.
The image of a permutation multiple of the distinguished vector is the auxiliary cardinality scalar times the vector of the inverse permutation.
The distinguished auxiliary vector has nonzero image under the linear map.
Defines an action of permutations on the first partition-indexed auxiliary type.
Acting by a permutation on the class of another permutation gives the class of their right product.
Assigns a natural-valued profile on `Fin n` to each permutation, indexed by a partition.
Equal permutation classes have equal natural-valued profiles.
A second auxiliary binary relation on permutations, indexed by a partition.
Maps a permutation to the first partition-indexed auxiliary type.
Two permutations have equal auxiliary classes exactly when their quotient product belongs to the indicated permutation collection.
Two permutations have equal auxiliary classes exactly when the indicated sorted-partition values agree at every finite index.
Permutations with equal natural-valued profiles have equal auxiliary classes.
The class of the permutation attached to a tableau agrees with the tableau's auxiliary class.
Taking a quotient representative and then its permutation class recovers the original class.
